title: Expected Behavior Curve for Evaluating Particle Counter Sampling Points in a Grade A Pharmaceutical Cleanroom: A Quality-by-Design Approach
content: Regulators require particle-counter sampling points in aseptic areas to be justified by risk assessment, yet no guideline provides a method to verify a location before routine use. This study proposes an expected behavior curve to test, at the design stage, whether a candidate sampling point responds to known disturbances as theory predicts. Candidate positions at different distances from the unidirectional-airflow outlet and from the critical point were tested in a Grade A area of an ophthalmic manufacturing plant, with and without curtain movement and operator approach. Measured particle counts were compared with a reference curve built from the expected effect of each factor and analyzed with a factorial design-of-experiments model. Only the position at an intermediate distance from the outlet and at the standard 30 cm (1 ft) from the critical point followed the reference curve while remaining within Grade A limits. Distance from the airflow outlet was the dominant factor; operator approach affected larger particles, whereas curtain movement had no significant effect. The expected behavior curve offers a simple, reproducible way to verify sampling-point representativeness before routine monitoring.
